@graph.headline: Options Trading Charges & STT in India: ₹63 a Lot
@graph.description: One NIFTY lot at ₹100 premium costs ~₹63 in total charges. Every line of the bill — STT, brokerage, exchange fees, GST, stamp duty — and the true breakeven.

mainEntity.name: How much does it cost to trade one NIFTY options lot in India?

acceptedAnswer.text: Buying and selling one NIFTY option lot at a ₹100 premium (lot size 65) costs roughly ₹63 in total charges — ₹26.53 on the buy leg and ₹36.08 on the sell leg, about ₹0.96 per share. Your exact number varies with the premium and your broker's plan, so estimate it before every trade.

mainEntity.name: Do I pay STT when buying options?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. STT on options is charged only when you sell — 0.15% of the premium, effective 1 April 2026. Stamp duty is the mirror image: 0.003% of premium turnover, charged on the buy side only.

mainEntity.name: What is STT on options trading in India?

acceptedAnswer.text: Two rates apply: 0.15% of the premium on the sale of an option, and 0.15% of the intrinsic value on an exercised option, paid by the purchaser. If the option expires worthless, there is no exercise and no exercise STT.

mainEntity.name: Which trading charges are the same at every broker?

acceptedAnswer.text: Almost everything except brokerage: STT, exchange transaction charges (0.03553% of premium on NSE), the SEBI turnover fee (₹10 per crore), stamp duty, and GST (18% on brokerage + exchange + SEBI charges) are set by the government, exchanges, and regulators. Only the brokerage itself varies — the discount-broker norm is a flat ~₹20 per executed order, while full-service brokers may charge a percentage.

mainEntity.name: What happens to charges if I let my option expire?

acceptedAnswer.text: If the option expires out of the money, it expires worthless — no sale leg, so no sale STT and no brokerage on exit. If it expires in the money and is exercised, STT of 0.15% applies on the intrinsic value, paid by the option holder — for deep in-the-money options this can be meaningful, so factor it in before deciding to hold into expiry.

mainEntity.name: Do intraday and positional option trades pay different charges?

acceptedAnswer.text: The charge structure is identical — same brokerage, same STT, same exchange and regulatory charges. What differs is the holding cost: positional trades may face overnight margin requirements, and any option held into expiry faces the exercise-STT question above.

mainEntity.name: How is STT calculated on options in India?

acceptedAnswer.text: Multiply the premium by 0.15% on the sale leg — one NIFTY lot at a ₹100 premium is ₹6,500 of premium, so the sale STT is ₹9.75. On an exercised option, STT is 0.15% of the intrinsic value, paid by the purchaser. There is no STT when you buy an option, and none if it expires worthless.
